'''''Stylosanthes biflora''''', known by the common names '''pencil flower''',<ref name="natureserve">{{cite web |title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0 |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.153884/Stylosanthes_biflora |website=explorer.natureserve.org}}</ref> '''sidebeak pencilflower''',<ref name="usda">{{PLANTS|id=STBI2|taxon=Stylosanthes biflora|accessdate=4 December 2015}}</ref> and '''endbeak pencilflower''',<ref name="NC">{{cite web |title=Stylosanthes biflora (Endbeak Pencilflower, Pencil Flower, Sidebeak Pencilflower) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/stylosanthes-biflora/ |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Fabaceae]] (legume) family. It is native to the [[Southeastern United States]] where it is widespread in open areas of native vegetation. It produces yellow-orange flowers in the summer and fall.

This species is highly variable throughout its range, and numerous species had previously been segregated out of it. However, their morphological differences have been found to be so overlapping that the former segregates are now considered the same species.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Robert H. Mohlenbrock | year = 1958 | title = The Stylosanthes biflora complex | jstor = 2483076 | journal = [[Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club]] | volume = 85 | pages = 341–346}}</ref>

==Description==
''S. biflora'' is a branching [[perennial]] that grows {{convert |4-12|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on|}} tall. The stems are wiry, round, hairy, and light to medium green. Each compound leaf has three leaflets ([[trifoliate]]) and are alternate on the stems. The leaflets measure {{convert |0.5-1.5|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on|}} long and are elliptic in shape. They have smooth margins. A pair of partly joined [[bracts]], or [[stipules]], tapering to a beak, surrounds the base of each [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] and part of the adjacent stem.<ref name="IL">{{cite web |title=Pencil Flower (Stylosanthes biflora) |url=https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/pencil_flw.html |website=www.illinoiswildflowers.info}}</ref> 

The flowers are orange to yellow and are similar to others in the pea family. The [[petals]] consist of large standard top) petal and smaller wings and keel, subtended by bracts.<ref name="MO">{{cite web |title=Pencil Flower |url=https://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/field-guide/pencil-flower |website=Missouri Department of Conservation |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pencil Flower |url=https://www.fs.usda.gov/wildflowers/plant-of-the-week/stylosanthes_biflora.shtml |website=www.fs.usda.gov}}</ref> The flowers are nearly circular in shape.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stylosanthes biflora page |url=https://www.missouriplants.com/Stylosanthes_biflora_page.html |website=www.missouriplants.com}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is native in the United States from Texas to the west, Illinois to the north, New York to the east, and Florida to the south. It is also present in Arizona.<ref name="natureserve"/> Its habitats include sunny and dry areas, such as glades, prairies, savannas, dry upland forests, tops of bluffs, and riverbanks.<ref name="MO"/>

==Ecology==
The flowers bloom May to September and are visited by bees and butterflies. It is a host plant for the barred yellow butterfly ([[Eurema daira]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=HOSTS - The Hostplants and Caterpillars Database at the Natural History Museum |url=https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/data/hostplants/search/list.dsml?searchPageURL=index.dsml&Familyqtype=starts+with&Family=&PFamilyqtype=starts+with&PFamily=&Genusqtype=starts+with&Genus=&PGenusqtype=starts+with&PGenus=stylosanthes&Speciesqtype=starts+with&Species=&PSpeciesqtype=starts+with&PSpecies=biflora&Country=&sort=Family |website=www.nhm.ac.uk}}</ref>
